introduction: An engagement session, sometimes called a pre-wedding session, is time set aside before the wedding to photograph the two of you together, away from the schedule and the guest list of the day itself. If you are looking for an engagement photographer or a pre-wedding photographer in London, Ontario, you are looking for the same session under two names, and this page explains how it works.
The photographs end up on save-the-dates, invitations and wedding websites, but the quieter benefit is practice: by the wedding day you will already know what it feels like to be photographed.

sections.heading: What the session is for
body: Most couples book an engagement session for a practical reason: they need photographs for a save-the-date card, printed invitations or a wedding website, and those deadlines are real. The reasons that keep people glad they booked arrive later. An afternoon spent being photographed together shows you what feels natural in front of a lens, where to put your hands, which of your jokes still makes you laugh, and what your partner looks like when they stop performing. Say how you plan to use the photographs when you book, because a card, a guest book and a website each want a different crop.

sections.heading: Choosing a place in London
body: London has river paths, old parks, market streets and campus lawns within a short drive of one another, so the useful question is less where is prettiest and more where are the two of you most yourselves. The park where you walk at weekends, the street of your first date or a spot near where you got engaged will relax you faster than any famous backdrop. The studio shoots engagement and pre-wedding sessions at [[CONFIRM: the locations the studio uses, from among these candidates: Wortley Village, Harris Park, Springbank Park, Fanshawe Pioneer Village, Gibbons Park, Victoria Park, the Covent Garden Market and downtown core, the Thames Valley Parkway, Western University's campus; also any travel fee outside London]].

sections.heading: Timing, seasons and the weather
body: Ontario's seasons change what is possible. Autumn colour along the river is brief, summer evenings stay light for hours, winter snow is beautiful but the afternoon is short and cold hands do not photograph well, and spring depends entirely on the week. Pick the season that matches the feeling you want, then check the printing deadline for your invitations before you pick the date. The busiest months for engagement bookings are [[CONFIRM: the months the studio is busiest]]. If the forecast turns on the day, [[CONFIRM: what the studio does in rain, cold or other bad weather]].

sections.heading: What to wear and what to bring
body: Wear clothes you could sit, walk and laugh in, in colours that sit comfortably together without matching. Solid, muted tones photograph more calmly than loud patterns or large logos, and shoes you can walk in matter more than they seem to. Bring water, a layer for when the light fades, and anything that belongs to the two of you as a pair, such as a dog, a bicycle or a favourite coffee. faqs.question: Is an engagement session the same as a pre-wedding session?
faqs.answer: Yes. Engagement and pre-wedding are two names for one session: time with the two of you before the wedding, usually used for invitations, a wedding website and keepsakes. Some couples say one word and some say the other, and it changes nothing about the session, the photographs or how you book it.

faqs.question: When should we book our engagement photos?
faqs.answer: Book before your invitation or save-the-date deadline, not just before the weather you want, because printing and mailing take longer than most couples expect. Choose the season you love first, then work backwards from the wedding date. The studio asks couples to book [[CONFIRM: how far ahead of the wedding date to book]]. Booking early also leaves room to move the session if the forecast is poor.

faqs.question: How long does it take to receive the photographs?
faqs.answer: Your package spells out which edited photographs and original images come with the session, so what you receive is settled when you book. When they arrive, and in what form, is [[CONFIRM: the delivery time and how photographs are delivered: online gallery, download or prints]]. If an invitation deadline is driving your date, mention it before you book.

faqs.question: What should we wear to an engagement session?
faqs.answer: Choose clothes you can sit, walk and laugh in, in colours that suit each of you without matching exactly. Avoid large logos and busy patterns, which compete with your faces, and look at the forecast so that you bring the right layer. Keep the outfits simple enough that you stop thinking about them within five minutes.

faqs.question: What happens if it rains on the day of our pre-wedding session?
faqs.answer: A light drizzle or flat grey cloud can suit portraits well, but heavy rain, strong wind or deep cold is a reason to move the session rather than endure it. [[CONFIRM: the studio's policy for rain and cold, including whether a deposit carries over to a new date]]. Look at the forecast the day before and write early if you are unsure.
